general: Most calories come from familiar cultivated grains, pulses, roots and oil crops descended from colonial agriculture. Managed livestock, fisheries, dairies and defended market gardens supply the ordinary table. Hunter-altered wildlife is not the population’s staple meat; wild carcasses require local inspection, and rare trophy flesh is no guarantee of safe food.

Cuisine follows climate, altitude, waterways, migration, former political unions and trade. National borders do not separate every recipe. Protected irrigation, terraces and greenhouses supply particular districts; they do not make every crop grow everywhere. Coffee, citrus, spices and good cooking oil may be imported luxuries far from their producing districts.

Smoking, salting, drying, fermenting and pickling are widespread. Canneries, commercial ice houses and some refrigerated warehouses exist at the established industrial level, but household refrigeration is uncommon. Freshness, butter, sugar, refined flour and meat portions reveal means and access more reliably than a dish’s name alone.

Public dining includes workers’ canteens, station kitchens, street stalls, inns, cafés, household suppers and formal court service. Meals can carry negotiation, affection, class distinctions, grief or scarcity without becoming a ceremony every time. The same broth can be generous at home and thin under rationing.

profiles.name: March of Veyrasse
profiles.history: Old coastal markets and the railway labour settlements exchange recipes with Caldrienne and Calvernis despite customs quarrels.
profiles.everyday: Ressant pot: white beans, leeks and barley, enriched with smoked pork when wages permit. Railway kitchens keep it warm for staggered shifts.
profiles.hospitality: Auvrienne veal in mustard cream, with buttered noodles; pear pastries follow at prosperous tables.
profiles.drink: Chicory coffee in workshops; real coffee, apple cider and dry valley wine in better-supplied houses.
profiles.daily_life: Fresh fish is ordinary near Serravonne, expensive uphill after a disrupted train. Station households stretch yesterday’s bread into broth dumplings.

profiles.name: Duchy of Caldrienne
profiles.history: Agricultural estates feed the northern arsenals; ducal kitchens and barracks draw on the same cattle and grain districts at very different prices.
profiles.everyday: Valdrec sour-pot: cabbage, potato and beef simmered with caraway; soldiers receive more cabbage and less beef.
profiles.hospitality: Roast goose with apple stuffing and buckwheat cakes, served at estate weddings and officers’ banquets.
profiles.drink: Dark malt beer; plum spirit poured in small glasses.
profiles.daily_life: Army purchasing can empty market stalls before a mobilisation. Housewives argue over whether a proper sour-pot should contain tomato, an imported coastal habit.

profiles.name: Karsenne Compact
profiles.history: Pass commerce carried dairy and grain dishes between otherwise stubbornly independent mining councils. Food is compact enough for a shift or a winter ascent.
profiles.everyday: Drossane cheese dumplings: stale bread, sharp mountain cheese and onion, browned and served in broth.
profiles.hospitality: Covered rye pie of smoked goat and mushrooms; the richest versions have a deep butter crust.
profiles.drink: Whey drinks and small beer during work; juniper spirit after the shift.
profiles.daily_life: Lower valleys supply potatoes and cabbage, upland pastures cheese. Bought flour and coastal salt become costly when freight negotiations fail.

profiles.name: Calvernis Republic
profiles.history: The banking ports absorbed recipes from their merchant crews, while inland households retained grain-and-bean cooking.
profiles.everyday: Miravelle fish pot: firm coastal fish, onions, white beans and wine broth, ladled over yesterday’s bread.
profiles.hospitality: Saffron rice with shellfish and a separately served herb oil; expensive spice marks a host’s means.
profiles.drink: Dry white wine, anise cordial and strong coffee.
profiles.daily_life: Dockside stalls sell fried small fish in paper. A merchant’s citrus preserves may have travelled farther than the guests eating them.

profiles.name: Ceralte Admiralty
profiles.history: Limited grain land and long sea passages made imported flour, preserved fish and safe drinking water matters of government.
profiles.everyday: Dalmor soaked biscuit: ship’s bread softened with fish broth, oil and onions; ashore it gains tomatoes and herbs.
profiles.hospitality: Whole baked rockfish under a salt crust, opened at the table; almond-and-citrus cakes for shore leave and family feasts.
profiles.drink: Weak beer, diluted island wine and lemon syrup when supplies allow.
profiles.daily_life: Islanders know several preparations of the same catch. Grain shortages change the size of a loaf before they change a naval ration.

profiles.name: Vardol
profiles.history: Refinery and arsenal towns share a strong canteen tradition with their farming hinterland. Winter provisions matter more inland than at the ports.
profiles.everyday: Rye parcels filled with potato, onion and smoked sausage, baked in communal ovens.
profiles.hospitality: Beef in dark beer with prune gravy and steamed bread; elaborate layered honey cake.
profiles.drink: Rye beer and sour cherry cordial.
profiles.daily_life: Shift whistles govern supper in the industrial wards. Kitchen gardens and pickled cabbage cushion disruptions to the grain trains.

profiles.name: Averholt
profiles.history: Provincial land bargains preserve different kitchens inside the same realm; grain taxes and shared fairs link the basins.
profiles.everyday: Barley risotto with mushrooms and hard cheese; peasant versions use dripping instead of butter.
profiles.hospitality: Stuffed river pike and pastry filled with poppy seed, served when a provincial house receives important guests.
profiles.drink: Apple wine in orchard districts; malt beer in the colder basins.
profiles.daily_life: Public ovens are meeting places as well as fuel economies. A dispute over milling rights can be discussed for an entire supper without anyone naming its political purpose.

profiles.name: Tervayne
profiles.history: Western ports face a different trading sea from Veyrasse and share more food traffic with southern islands and Otrantian merchants.
profiles.everyday: Fish-and-potato bake beneath an oat crust, with pickled onions.
profiles.hospitality: Mussels in cream and white wine, followed by baked custard scented with imported spice.
profiles.drink: Coastal cider, amber beer and port-house coffee.
profiles.daily_life: Sailors’ inexpensive meals favour salted fish; fresh shellfish signals a short journey from water to table. Inland villages are less maritime than the national reputation suggests.

profiles.name: Serevask Republic
profiles.history: The old Serevask customs federation joined four southern basins, never Vesalius as a whole. Its divided successors still recognise one another’s dishes.
profiles.everyday: Serevask sour rice: rice and lentils finished with soured milk, toasted seed and browned onion.
profiles.hospitality: Duck with bitter orange, accompanied by layered rice scented with preserved peel.
profiles.drink: Strong black tea; fermented rice drink at harvest gatherings.
profiles.daily_life: The remnant government maintains public grain kitchens near its ministries. Former federal recipes outlast the tax union, while each successor claims its own version is the original.

profiles.name: Varnelle
profiles.history: Delta rice, fisheries and freight markets furnished the former federation’s export table; incoming crews introduced sour, hot and sweet condiments.
profiles.everyday: Varnelle red rice with river fish, pepper and beans, cooked in one broad pan.
profiles.hospitality: Crab broth with fine rice noodles and citrus leaf; confectioners sell sesame brittle.
profiles.drink: Iced citrus water where ice can be bought; tea and light cane spirit.
profiles.daily_life: Fish sauce is an everyday seasoning rather than a luxury. Flood years alter rice prices across all four successor states.

profiles.name: Kelbrun
profiles.history: Upriver gardens and plantation labour communities mix basin rice dishes with tubers, legumes and orchard fruit.
profiles.everyday: Steamed tuber cakes with black beans and a sharp herb relish.
profiles.hospitality: Pork braised in cane syrup and sour fruit; rice cakes filled with ground nuts for festivals.
profiles.drink: Roasted-grain coffee substitutes and cane spirit; estate houses serve imported coffee.
profiles.daily_life: Labourers eat at field shelters from wrapped parcels. Plantation owners’ lavish fruit tables conceal the uneven access to meat and purchased grain.

profiles.name: Gavrel
profiles.history: March-house kitchens descend from basin customs but favour portable grain and smoked provisions for retainers travelling between estates.
profiles.everyday: Millet cakes with goat stew and sour plum relish.
profiles.hospitality: Spit-roasted kid with nut paste, followed by dense dried-fruit bread.
profiles.drink: Sour milk, herbal tea and plum wine.
profiles.daily_life: Hospitality includes bread broken by the host, but its quality distinguishes an honoured guest from a hired messenger. Poor tenants substitute lentils for goat.

profiles.name: Veldrassen
profiles.history: A composite crown includes humid lowlands, high terraces and temperate uplands; formal court service conceals many provincial kitchens.
profiles.everyday: Maize polenta with beans and mushroom gravy in the uplands; rice replaces maize in irrigated lowland districts.
profiles.hospitality: Braised beef with red wine and layered herb pasta; provincial delegates insist on different cheeses.
profiles.drink: Plateau beer, lowland cane drink and coffee at the court.
profiles.daily_life: Altitude matters as much as latitude. Mountain towns import much of their grain, while court menus display produce from every province as a claim to unity.

profiles.name: Ostrevain
profiles.history: Cereal estates, cattle districts and newly industrial towns trade large quantities of durable staples. Central purchasing has spread army dishes across provincial boundaries.
profiles.everyday: Pepper bean stew thickened with maize meal, with smoked beef on paydays.
profiles.hospitality: Stuffed roast fowl, squash dumplings and nut pastries.
profiles.drink: Brown beer and lightly fermented fruit drinks.
profiles.daily_life: Soldiers carry toasted grain and hard cheese; wealthy tables emphasise fresh meat and fruit that has not endured a convoy journey.

profiles.name: Rovessara
profiles.history: Maritime commerce joins a mild western coast to upland cheese districts and distant spice markets. Restaurant fashion changes faster than village food.
profiles.everyday: Bean-and-greens soup with flatbread and olive oil; tiny fried fish at the quays.
profiles.hospitality: Rice cooked in seafood stock, fine stuffed pasta and chilled fruit creams in wealthy city cafés.
profiles.drink: Bitter coffee, aperitif wine and citrus cordial.
profiles.daily_life: Fresh oil, mountain butter and imported spice coexist rather than defining one uniform national cuisine. Ice houses and refrigerated warehouses support the richest urban tables.

profiles.name: Brannervaux
profiles.history: Unequal river cities share barges, mill customs and periodic floods. Grain, pulses and freshwater fish travel more readily than political loyalty.
profiles.everyday: Lentils with smoked carp and flat noodles; poorer bowls omit fish and add greens.
profiles.hospitality: River-fish dumplings in herb butter and plum-filled pastries.
profiles.drink: Pear cider, mild beer and roasted-barley drinks.
profiles.daily_life: Floodplain gardens supply onions and beans. Fish smoking and grain warehouses make the river ports vital even to communities beyond the floodplain.

profiles.name: Cervaud
profiles.history: Border garrisons borrow cooking from both larger patrons, while local families argue over which dishes predate foreign influence.
profiles.everyday: Cabbage rolls stuffed with rice or barley and a little minced meat.
profiles.hospitality: Roast pork with sour cherries and crisp potato cakes.
profiles.drink: Dark beer, cherry spirit and heavily sweetened coffee for visitors.
profiles.daily_life: Ration bread and pickled vegetables dominate remote posts. Market-day sausages are a small luxury that survives frequent changes of uniform.

profiles.name: Veylac
profiles.history: Industrial towns link cooler uplands to river farms. Working households value meals that can be reheated when factory shifts end at different hours.
profiles.everyday: Baked beans beneath an onion-and-breadcrumb crust, with smoked sausage when affordable.
profiles.hospitality: Cheese-filled pasta browned in butter; orchard-fruit tart at civic dinners.
profiles.drink: Pale beer, plum cordial and café coffee.
profiles.daily_life: Cooperative dining rooms compete with private factory canteens. Imported coastal fish is popular but more expensive than the local root-and-grain staples.

profiles.name: Ossavren successor territories
profiles.history: Former royal roads carried recipes across a realm now divided by customs barriers and rival armies. Shared dishes remain a language of kinship across hostile borders.
profiles.everyday: Red lentil pot with flatbread in warm valleys; barley-and-turnip broth in higher districts.
profiles.hospitality: Lamb with preserved lemon and almonds; former court households still serve rosewater rice pudding.
profiles.drink: Mint tea in warm valleys, mountain beer inland and sweet wine in surviving vineyard districts.
profiles.daily_life: Smuggling brings salt, oil and family recipes across front lines. An abundant banquet may conceal shortages in a neighbouring claimant’s territory.

profiles.name: Rovengard
profiles.history: Sheltered southern valleys support oats, rye, roots and dairy herds; forest preserves add berries and inspected game.
profiles.everyday: Rye-crust fish loaf with potato and onion, carried cold or warmed beside a stove.
profiles.hospitality: Venison with sour red berries and cream, followed by baked curd cheese.
profiles.drink: Small beer, berry cordial and hot herb infusions.
profiles.daily_life: A winter pantry matters more than a fashionable fresh ingredient. Household drying racks and communal bake days bind city relatives to valley farms.

profiles.name: Varnesk
profiles.history: Mining leagues inherit northern preservation techniques but rely heavily on imported grain and valley dairy produce.
profiles.everyday: Potato-and-rye dumplings with smoked pork and fermented cabbage.
profiles.hospitality: Beef baked beneath a thick salt-and-rye crust, opened for foundry feasts.
profiles.drink: Dark rye beer; strong black tea bought through concession merchants.
profiles.daily_life: Canteens portion meat by shift entitlement. A late supply train can turn dumplings into thin flour soup without stopping the furnaces.

profiles.name: Galdresk
profiles.history: Order houses preserve remedies and practical cookery alongside the older arts. Most food is ordinary, nourishing and carefully stored.
profiles.everyday: Oat broth with roots, mushrooms and dried fish; kitchens adjust texture for the sick.
profiles.hospitality: Trout in cream with dill-like herbs, served with small sourdough loaves and berry compote.
profiles.drink: Unsweetened herbal tea and berry wine on feast days.
profiles.daily_life: Healing traditions do not make every herb magical. Supplies are dated and inspected; winter hospitality can impose a serious obligation on an isolated house.

profiles.name: Halskert
profiles.history: Seasonal river traffic sustains mills, fisheries and gardens in comparatively sheltered valleys. Boat families carry recipes between rival towns.
profiles.everyday: Barley baked with lake fish and onion in covered crocks.
profiles.hospitality: Butter-fried freshwater fish, green peas and a layered berry cake during the short summer.
profiles.drink: Oat beer and tart orchard cider where fruit grows.
profiles.daily_life: Smokehouses fill before freeze-up. Spring fish suppers mark reopened navigation and the arrival of news as much as the season’s catch.

profiles.name: Bellacosta Cantons
profiles.everyday: Rice cooked in coconut milk accompanies peppered fish near the coast; inland labourers eat cassava cakes and bean relish. At Jougrenne, prosperous hosts serve fish wrapped in aromatic leaves, followed by cane syrup fritters. Sour fruit drinks and weak cane beer are ordinary; imported wine belongs to charter banquets.

profiles.name: Cavressa Principalities
profiles.everyday: Barley noodles with browned cabbage are everyday food in the cooler districts. Shepherds carry hard cheese and sour rye loaves; court cooks serve mutton with dried plums and a crust of toasted grain. Albaret inns are known for pear pastries. Dark beer and plum spirit travel better than fresh milk.

profiles.name: Vaulcerre Basin Leagues
profiles.everyday: Millet porridge with greens and groundnut sauce feeds field crews; fish dried beside the canals enriches stews. Jarnan serves spiced rice with river fish on market days. Fermented grain drink is inexpensive, while sweet tea signals a household with access to imported leaves. Drought changes recipes before it changes official water allocations.

profiles.name: Seravelle Littoral
profiles.everyday: Astrellac cooks fish in tomato and fennel broth and lays yesterday’s bread beneath it. Bean-filled pastries and olives travel inland with merchants. Wealthy harbour tables add citrus-roasted poultry and almond cakes; dockworkers buy chickpea fritters. Coastal wine is plentiful locally, while coffee is sold in small, strong cups.

profiles.name: Haldrevik Concessions
profiles.everyday: Workers eat oat flatbread, pea soup and smoked fish at company canteens. Mushroom pies and berry preserves mark a well-stocked household. Managers import white flour and wine for renewal dinners; crews drink malt beer or roasted-grain coffee. An interrupted supply convoy can make the company shop the only source of food and deepen wage debt.

profiles.name: Dreissen Wardholds
profiles.everyday: Rye-and-oat bread, dried fish and sour cabbage dominate fortress kitchens. Venison is a costly addition to barley stew, not an everyday entitlement. Festival tables offer potato dumplings with browned butter and tart berry sauce. Hot malt drinks and strong grain spirit accompany winter hospitality; fuel scarcity limits baking as much as flour scarcity does.

profiles.name: Varneselle Estates
profiles.everyday: Fish baked under a rye crust is shared along the shore; inland tables favour potato cakes with cultured cream and mushrooms. A formal estate meal adds roast poultry and sour-berry pudding. Small beer accompanies workday suppers, while herb spirits are offered to guests. The port’s fresh bread distinguishes it from outlying households that bake only when fuel permits.

profiles.name: Bressavelle Marches
profiles.everyday: Households bake bean-and-onion pies and stretch broth with torn bread. Market inns serve pork with apples and coarse mustard; better tables add freshwater fish in butter and herb sauce. Cider is common in orchard districts, ale elsewhere. Customs officers are notorious for accepting imported coffee as hospitality while charging duty on the next sack.

profiles.name: Vallessia Cantons
profiles.everyday: Rice-and-bean dishes with sharp green relish are common in the warmer cantons; upland tables add maize bread and soft cheese. Galigny market stalls sell stuffed peppers when in season. Feast days bring roast poultry with sour fruit, and sweet fritters. Light beer and fruit cordials are ordinary; imported coffee is concentrated in commercial houses.

profiles.name: Rivessac Coast
profiles.everyday: Coastal kitchens combine fish, white beans, garlic and local greens; inland families make herb dumplings and barley bread. Saultac’s market speciality is poultry braised with olives and sour citrus. Hosts offer almond biscuits with coffee when they can afford it; diluted wine or herbal infusions are more usual. Fresh fish becomes a luxury only a short disrupted journey inland.

profiles.history: Terrace farms and convoy stores support distinct island kitchens; mainland warehouses introduced flour and coffee.
profiles.everyday: Barley cakes with bean stew, smoked fish and orchard chutney.
profiles.hospitality: Roast lamb with sour fruit and honeyed pears.
profiles.drink: Small beer and dry orchard cider.
profiles.daily_life: Fresh water is served before wine at a guest meal; a full jug signals a household willing to share its cistern.
profiles.name: Varessan Sea League

profiles.history: Older island farming overlaps with settler orchards and export estates.
profiles.everyday: Bean-and-root stew, grilled fish and flat bread.
profiles.hospitality: Citrus-braised poultry, stuffed vegetables and orchard tarts.
profiles.drink: Fruit wine, cane spirit and imported coffee.
profiles.daily_life: Company dining rooms and village kitchens use the same crops but distribute the best produce differently.
profiles.name: Talascan Charter Islands

profiles.history: Terraced grain and sheltered orchards developed alongside merchant seafaring.
profiles.everyday: Steamed barley with beans, greens and fish broth.
profiles.hospitality: Herb-crusted fish, roast kid and nut pastries.
profiles.drink: Grain beer and spiced pear wine.
profiles.daily_life: Outer households preserve more fish and dairy; the capital displays produce from across the compacts.
profiles.name: Nemerai Crown

profiles.history: Cold-water fishing and mixed farming supply households and passing ships.
profiles.everyday: Oat broth with smoked fish, turnips and buttered bread.
profiles.hospitality: Mutton pie with leeks and baked apples.
profiles.drink: Oat ale and berry cordial.
profiles.daily_life: Winter smokehouses and communal grain stores remain important even where imported tins are fashionable.
profiles.name: Ordelune Overseas Districts

profiles.history: Collective stores and rescue obligations shape the table.
profiles.everyday: Fish-and-barley broth with turnips and hard cheese.
profiles.hospitality: Slow-cooked mutton and berry cakes at assemblies.
profiles.drink: Weak malt ale and hot berry infusions.
profiles.daily_life: Visitors eat from a host hearth’s stores; prolonged stays create reciprocal obligations.
profiles.name: Skeldran Hearth Confederacy

profiles.history: Port commerce brought varied seasonings to island farming and fisheries.
profiles.everyday: Bean soup, fish cakes and pickled greens.
profiles.hospitality: Wine-braised lamb, stuffed squash and citrus custard.
profiles.drink: Dry wine, pale beer and imported coffee.
profiles.daily_life: Dockside houses advertise fixed-price meals; wealthy tables display fresh produce from distant islands.
profiles.name: Merovian Island Republic

profiles.history: Wet-valley cultivation and reef fisheries support inter-island exchanges.
profiles.everyday: Rice or steamed roots with beans and fish in sour fruit broth.
profiles.hospitality: Leaf-wrapped poultry, shellfish and sweet root cakes.
profiles.drink: Fermented rice drink and fruit infusions.
profiles.daily_life: Communal feasts affirm obligations between councils; everyday cooking varies by island.
profiles.name: Ashalai Reef Covenant

profiles.history: A maritime court draws on irrigated valleys, plantation districts and fishing towns.
profiles.everyday: Rice with bean gravy, greens and salted fish.
profiles.hospitality: Fruit-braised pork, fragrant rice and layered sugar cakes.
profiles.drink: Cane spirit, light beer and imported tea.
profiles.daily_life: Mill workers buy meals near the gates; court hospitality prizes fresh produce from several islands.
profiles.name: Kingdom of Istrana

profiles.history: Settler dairy farms and older fishing communities exchange food across distinct land systems.
profiles.everyday: Rye bread, fish soup, cabbage and cheese.
profiles.hospitality: Roast goose or fish pie with sour berries.
profiles.drink: Rye ale and juniper-flavoured spirits.
profiles.daily_life: Northern stations ration imported flour through winter; southern markets offer more variety.
profiles.name: Edrask Governorate

profiles.history: Seasonal travel and reciprocal refuge duties shape storage and hospitality.
profiles.everyday: Fish broth, preserved meat and coarse grain cakes.
profiles.hospitality: Slow-cooked herd meat with roots and berries.
profiles.drink: Hot herb infusions and occasional imported ale.
profiles.daily_life: Stored food is carefully accounted for because rescue hospitality and winter survival draw on the same reserves.
profiles.name: Norrakai Moots
